question: An introductory statement in a constitution that states the reasons and guiding values of the constitution is called:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Preamble**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Preamble is an introductory statement in a constitution that states the reasons and guiding values of the document.
 
• It serves as a brief introduction to the principles and philosophy underlying the constitution.
 
• The Preamble reflects the vision and objectives that the constitution aims to achieve.
 
• In many countries, the Preamble is considered a key component as it sets the tone and purpose of the constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Clause:**

 
 
• A clause in a constitution refers to a specific provision or section that addresses a particular point or issue.
 
• Clauses are often used to detail the powers, duties, and rights within the constitution.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights:**
 
 
• Fundamental rights are the basic human rights guaranteed to all citizens by the constitution.
 
• These rights are essential for the protection of individual liberties and the promotion of social justice.
 
 
 
• **Article:**
 
 
• An article in a constitution is a major division that sets out specific laws or principles.
 
• Articles are used to systematically organize the content of the constitution into manageable sections.
